summary: The selected papers emphasize jet substructure and color decoherence, microscopic relaxation beyond viscosity matching, low-energy baryon stopping and isospin conversion, magnetic-field effects during pre-equilibrium, and physics ML methods for nuclear cross-section transfer learning and bottomonium suppression. The strongest items are the jet-quenching/EEC pair and the kinetic-relaxation paper; the main caution concerns proceedings-level evidence for strangeness-sensitive stopping ratios.
strongest_paper_summary: arXiv:2609.05609 and arXiv:2609.05614 form the strongest heavy-ion theme, using energy-energy correlators and jet nuclear modification to probe QGP color decoherence and medium resolution.

papers.title: The Colors of Jet Quenching
papers.short_authors: Hannah Bossi, Maxence Larose, Yacine Mehtar-Tani
papers.abstract: The paper combines inclusive jet nuclear modification factors with energy-energy correlators to extract quark and gluon quenching factors and a medium resolution scale, finding that color decoherence improves the description of heavy-ion jet data.

papers.title: Energy-energy correlators and color decoherence from a generating functional
papers.abstract: A leading-log generating-functional framework gives coupled evolution equations for jet RAA and EECs, including coherent-to-incoherent evolution in the large-Nc limit.

papers.title: Beyond Viscosity Matching: Microscopic Relaxation in Anisotropic Flow
papers.abstract: The paper argues that dilute anisotropic flow in small collision systems probes a spectrum of microscopic angular relaxation rates, not only the quadrupole rate encoded by shear viscosity.

papers.title: Effective kinetic theory description of the magnetic field-induced anisotropic gluon pressure during pre-equilibrium in heavy-ion collisions
papers.short_authors: Khwahish Kushwah, Alejandro Ayala, Gabriel S. Denicol, Ana Mizher
papers.abstract: A Boltzmann-Vlasov model is used to estimate how time-dependent magnetic fields affect early gluon pressure anisotropy during the collisionless pre-equilibrium stage.

papers.title: Microscopic study of baryon stopping in low-energy heavy-ion collisions within UrQMD model
papers.abstract: UrQMD interaction histories in Au+Au collisions from sqrt(sNN)=2.4-17.3 GeV are used to classify stopped protons and quantify a large isospin-converted component relevant to FAIR/NICA energies.

papers.title: A phenomenological approach to direct K* production and hadronic medium effects in nucleus-nucleus collisions at high baryon density
papers.short_authors: Hongcan Li, Yun Liu, Guangyu Zheng, Yaping Wang, Guannan Xie, Gao-chan Yong
papers.abstract: AMPT-HC is extended with a tunable direct K* production component to study K*/K centrality trends, daughter rescattering, and reconstruction efficiency in Au+Au at 3 GeV.

papers.title: Inclusive electron-nucleus cross section models from domain adaptation
papers.short_authors: Krzysztof M. Graczyk, Beata E. Kowal, Rwik Dharmapal Banerjee, Jose Luis Bonilla, Hemant Prasad, Jan T. Sobczyk
papers.abstract: Transfer learning adapts carbon-trained neural-network ensembles to multiple nuclear targets while studying layer depth, training coverage, target dependence, and comparison to F1F2 phenomenology.

papers.title: Bottomonium suppression with a machine-learning-informed Debye mass
papers.short_authors: Ajaharul Islam, Shibo Chen, Fu-Peng Li, Long-Gang Pang, Guang-You Qin
papers.abstract: An ML-informed Debye mass from lattice-informed inputs is inserted into a complex KSU heavy-quark potential and used with QTraj to compute Upsilon suppression in Pb-Pb collisions.

cautions.title: The role of strangeness in baryon and electric charge stoppings
cautions.abstract: A proceedings contribution argues that baryon-to-charge stopping ratios are sensitive to strange-antistrange and light-quark rapidity distributions and highlights tension with STAR isobar data.
